ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: All first year candidates for undergraduate admission must submit the following: Common Application or our UNewHaven Application, $50 Application Fee, Official High School Transcript (Unofficial are acceptable to complete the application process, but official transcripts will be required for enrolling students), and an Essay (250-650 words). A Letter of Recommendation is optional. [2]
Concentration: ['General Concentration', 'Applied History and Public Policy Concentration']
Description: As a history major at the University of New Haven, you will develop an in-depth understanding of how the seminal events that preceded us impacted us then and how they affect our society today and moving forward. The field of history is one of the central disciplines of the liberal arts and it provides a classic mode of learning. [13] At its core, history deals with real people and events, and it offers limitless opportunities for intensive exploration. You learn through class discussions, debates and a senior thesis project; have the opportunity to study abroad for a semester; take elective courses that allow you to customize your course of study based on your interests; or double major or minor in a complementary field of study. You'll also develop your critical thinking, research, and writing skills, and gain an education in logic and reasoning. [13] Students in the B.A. History program - General concentration must complete 121 credits. [12] The B.A. History - Applied History and Public Policy Concentration requires the completion of 121 credits. [3]
Accredidation: The University of New Haven is accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE). [9, 10] Accreditation by the Commission applies to the institution as a whole and is not a guarantee of every course or program offered. [10] No specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Arts in History program is mentioned on the university's website.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Homeland Security
Department: Henry C. Lee College of Criminal Justice and Forensic Sciences
Description: Homeland security is a broad discipline within the field of national security. It is a combination of law enforcement, defense, immigration policy, and counter-terrorism policy — the primary areas that affect the security of the nation. With the University of New Haven's B.S. in Homeland Security program, you will understand how to prevent and disrupt attacks on the American people and critical infrastructure and ensure seamless integration between multiple levels of government. Our country faces ongoing threats, including extremism, terrorism, and cyber attacks. By studying homeland security, you'll learn to protect the well-being of the nation and its citizens and develop the leadership qualities that are needed when disaster strikes.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality & Tourism Management
Requirements: All first year candidates for undergraduate admission must submit the following: Common Application or our UNewHaven Application, $50 Application Fee, Official High School Transcript, and an Essay (250-650 words). A Letter of Recommendation is optional. [2]
Concentration: ['General Concentration', 'Hotel and Resort Management', 'Event and Tourism Management']
Description: People are traveling the country and the world as never before, so there's a serious need for professionals who can make them feel welcome when they reach their destination. At the University of New Haven, you'll pair big-picture business knowledge with industry-specific skills (even the art of wine appreciation) to become a world-class expert in hospitality and tourism management. To focus your education and chart your future career path, you'll choose one of three concentrations: General Concentration; Hotel and Resort Management; Event and Tourism Management. You'll Also: Learn front-office skills, including sales, marketing, accounting, purchasing, housekeeping, and maintenance; Expand your knowledge into areas of culinary arts, guest services, and event planning. Take field trips to conventions and trade shows. Gain hands-on experience through an internship. Have the opportunity to study abroad. Work directly with faculty and staff on hospitality-related events and projects, such as managing the University of New Haven's on-campus café and catering University events. Spend a day with hospitality industry executives.
Accredidation: The College of Business at the University of New Haven, which houses the Hospitality and Tourism Management program, is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial & Systems Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Industrial and Systems Engineering at the University of New Haven is a highly interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for the "big picture" challenges in various systems. [3, 4] Industrial and systems engineers focus on ensuring large systems, such as transportation, food-supply, and communication, run smoothly by improving efficiency and cost-effectiveness. [4] The program's objectives are to prepare graduates who will be gainfully engaged in the professional practice of systems or industrial engineering, contribute to complex projects in multidisciplinary environments, advance their skills through lifelong learning, and be involved in the leadership of their profession and society. [3] Students learn to apply mathematics and science to design engineering systems, conduct experiments, analyze and interpret data, and design components or processes to meet needs within realistic constraints like economic, environmental, social, and ethical factors. [4] IMPORTANT: The university website states that this program is no longer accepting applications. [4]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Industrial and Systems Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org. [3, 8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Intelligence Analysis
Requirements: All first year candidates for undergraduate admission must submit the following: Common Application or our UNewHaven Application, $50 Application Fee, Official High School Transcript (Unofficial are acceptable to complete the application process, but official transcripts will be required for enrolling students), and an Essay (250-650 words; the application essay meets this requirement). A letter of recommendation is listed as optional. [5]
Department: Henry C. Lee College of Criminal Justice and Forensic Sciences
Description: The Intelligence Analysis degree reflects the continually evolving nature of intelligence analysis, with an emphasis on teaching the necessary academic knowledge and analytical skills students will need in the assessment and collection, correlation, and analysis of intelligence data, especially relating to national security, law enforcement, military, or business intelligence. [7]
ScholarshipAmount: $15,000 - $33,000 per academic year
ScholarshipPercentage: A 50% Tuition Scholarship is available to graduating high school students from West Haven. [2]

ScholarshipType: The University of New Haven offers merit-based scholarships, need-based grants such as the Federal Pell Grant and University Grant-in-Aid, and college access partnership scholarships. [27, 29, 31]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Interior Design & Pre-Architecture
Requirements: The University of New Haven's website states that the admission process for undergraduate programs can begin as early as the end of a student's high school junior year. They offer both full-time and part-time opportunities for domestic and international students. Description: As a University of New Haven interior design major you will learn to create beautiful, functional spaces that meet the needs of both individual and business clients. [2] The knowledge and skills you acquire in the program and the opportunities offered include: Successfully mastering the rules of proportion, scale, balance, contrast, color, texture, rhythm, and harmony. [2] Learning to manipulate architecture to create a more effective use of space. Focusing on issues of sustainability and universal design. [2] Developing an understanding of environmental factors including acoustics, lighting, the use of space, and temperature control. [2]
Accredidation: The University of New Haven interior design program leading to the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Interior Design with a General or Pre-Architecture concentration is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation, www.accredit-id.org, 206 Cesar E. [2] This mark of excellence designates the University's B.A. in Art and B.F.A. programs in Graphic and Digital Design, and Interior Design as nationally accredited programs. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Affairs

The program places a unique emphasis on the development of transferrable job skills such as critical thinking, interpersonal communication, cultural understanding and adaptiveness, writing, problem-solving, persuasion, and public speaking. Studentswilldevelopmasteryofcontentareasinthefieldsofpoliticalandeconomicdevelopment,nationalsecurity,anddiplomacy.Inaddition,theprogramplacesaparticularemphasis on the role of women in economic and political development and the necessity for sustainable economic and environmental socio-politico systems. Graduates will be well-positioned for work with national governments, international organizations, the private sector, think tanks, non-governmental organizations, multi-national corporations, or further graduate study at top-tier programs. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in International Business
Requirements: The University of New Haven's official website does not provide a centralized, general list of application requirements at the institute level. Requirements are typically specified at the program level.
Description: As an international business major at the University of New Haven, you'll gain a global perspective through interdisciplinary studies in the core principles of accounting, economics, finance, management and marketing. You'll also become proficient in a foreign language and participate in a study abroad experience that will enable you to thrive in any global business environment. [12] You'll study the economic, geographic, historical, legal, regulatory and political factors that influence international trade, business and investment. [12] You will also learn strategies for entering foreign markets including exporting, licensing, and strategic alliances; learn to manage cultural differences and organize international negotiations; develop ethical decision-making skills within a global context; and understand international capital markets and financial, political and economic risk. [12]
Accredidation: AACSB accreditation means that our Pompea College of Business has passed a rigorous set of standards. The faculty, students, programs and research have been closely examined and judged to be of exceptionally high standards. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Legal Studies
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission at the University of New Haven, applicants must submit the Common Application, an official high school transcript, and one letter of recommendation. The university has a test-optional policy for most programs.
Department: Henry C. Lee College of Criminal Justice and Forensic Sciences
Description: Law governs our society, from the sublime principles in the U.S. Constitution through the regulations that govern the food we eat and the water we drink. But with laws, also come disputes. Today, there are forms of dispute resolution that didn't exist years ago. To further complicate things, globalization is blurring the lines between national and international law. Legal policy is going to shape the future. The goal of our legal studies programs is to prepare you for every success in it. Your program is flexible and interdisciplinary. You can combine your legal studies with programs in other areas such as criminal justice, business, accounting, political science, psychology, or global studies. A two-semester internship in your final year lets you back up your classroom learning with on-the-job experience, which opens up more employment doors for you. Want to see the world? An international track lets you study for a semester abroad to satisfy concentration requirements.
Accredidation: The American Bar Association-approved options include the Bachelor's Degree Concentration in Paralegal Studies. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Legal Studies, Public Affairs Concentration

The University of New Haven offers a comprehensive financial aid program, with students receiving assistance in the form of grants, scholarships, student loans, and part-time employment. More than 85 percent of the University's full-time undergraduate students receive some form of financial assistance. [16]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marine & Environmental Sciences
Department: Henry C. Lee College of Criminal Justice and Forensic Sciences
Description: Humans are inextricably linked with the world's oceans and coasts. For the world's populations, these ecosystems have always served as sources of food, medicine, energy, commerce, education, recreation, and well-being. This program will give you a more profound knowledge of this interconnectedness through a multidisciplinary approach grounded in biological and earth sciences, social science, and policy. As one of the most complex coastal estuarine systems in the world, Long Island Sound is a marine and environmental scientist's paradise — and that paradise is only minutes from the University of New Haven campus. As you immerse yourself in the program and in the many field trips to these ecosystems, you will learn about all of the world's oceans, terrestrial, and marine environments and organisms, and the fascinating ways humans interact with them.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marketing
Requirements: All first-year candidates for undergraduate admission must submit the following: a completed Common Application or UNewHaven Application, a $50 application fee, and an official high school transcript. An essay of 250-650 words is also required. A letter of recommendation is listed as optional.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Marketing program at the University of New Haven is housed within the AACSB-accredited Pompea College of Business, a distinction that places it among the top six percent of business schools globally. [8] The program provides students with opportunities for hands-on learning, such as creating Google AdWords campaigns for real clients and studying abroad at the university's Tuscany, Italy campus. [8] Students can also participate in the University's chapter of the American Marketing Association, which facilitates networking with industry leaders. [8] The curriculum offers a Fast Track program option, allowing students to complete their B.S. in three years or a combined B.S. and MBA in four years (3+1). [8]
Accredidation: The Pompea College of Business at the University of New Haven has been accredited by The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) since 2015, with a renewal in 2025 that extends through the 2030-2031 academic year. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marketing, General Concentration
Requirements: All first year candidates for undergraduate admission must submit the following: Common Application or our UNewHaven Application, a $50 Application Fee, an official High School Transcript, and an essay (250-650 words). A letter of recommendation is optional. [2]
Description: As a Bachelor of Science in Marketing major at the University of New Haven, you will complement a strong foundation in the principles of business by specializing in how e-commerce and marketing technologies such as social media, database marketing, Google AdWords, and data mining have impacted – and forever changed – the traditional study and practice of marketing. [13] You'll also learn about modern competitive strategies, development processes, consumer research and distribution channels, explore advertising and international marketing, and gain real-world experience through a supervised practicum or internship. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marketing, Marketing Analytics Concentration
Requirements: The general application requirements for first-year candidates include submitting the Common Application or the UNewHaven Application, a $50 application fee, an official high school transcript, and an essay of 250-650 words. [9, 10] A letter of recommendation is considered optional for most applicants but is required for international students. [3, 10] International students must also submit official certified copies of their senior secondary/high school records and may need to provide proof of English proficiency. [3]
Description: Students earning a B.S. degree in marketing are required to complete 121 credits, including the university core curriculum (40 credits) and the business program core. [7] The Pompea College of Business Core consists of 30 credits and includes courses such as Introduction to Financial Accounting, Principles of Marketing, and Business Capstone. [7] The major requires 18 credits in courses like Organizational Marketing, International Marketing, and Digital Marketing. [7] The Marketing Analytics Concentration requires an additional 9 credits in Data Mining, Customer Database Marketing, and Social Media Marketing. [7]
Accredidation: The business programs at the University of New Haven's Pompea College of Business are accredited by AACSB, which places the University among the top 5% of business schools globally. [4] The Marketing undergraduate program is listed as one of the AACSB-accredited programs at the University of New Haven. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Description: Math is everywhere, from the spiral of a shell to the timing of a symphony, and it is integral to everything around us. As a mathematics major at the University of New Haven, you’ll apply math’s universal language to your area of interest, while sharpening your ability to reason and problem solve. Through the B.S. program, you will: Prepare for a wide variety of careers, such as being a computer consultant, statistical analyst, scientific research analyst, product manager, educator, or business manager. Learn from professors who are dedicated to your success. Our faculty are leaders and innovators in their fields, bringing both deep professional experience and academic rigor to the classroom.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: Applicants are evaluated based on a comprehensive review of their application, which includes a holistic assessment of their academic background. This takes into account the rigor of their high school coursework, grade trends, and cumulative unweighted GPA. [1] While there are no specific minimum GPA or test scores required for admission, successful applicants typically demonstrate strong academic achievement. [1]
Description: Mechanical engineering encompasses a diverse and ever-expanding range of disciplines, focusing on the analysis, design, and testing of machines, products, and systems that are essential to modern life. From everyday objects like doorknobs, tennis rackets, and fishing reels, to complex technologies like power plants, skyscrapers, and electric vehicles, mechanical engineers are at the forefront of innovation. In the University of New Haven's ABET-accredited B.S. in Mechanical Engineering program you will join that long line of pioneers, using your skills to design, analyze, improve, and test the products and systems that are essential to everyday life -- and to create those that don't yet exist. [2] Through our program, you'll build a multidisciplinary foundation in mechanical, chemical, civil, and electrical engineering and develop skills in physics, chemistry, and mathematics as well. [2]
Accredidation: The B.S. program in Mechanical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Mechanical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science
Requirements: The University of New Haven is a test-optional institution. For admission to the Medical Laboratory Science program, students are required to have a high school diploma or GED, with a preferred GPA of 3.0 or higher. A strong background in science (biology and chemistry) and math is also preferred. The application is submitted through the Common Application.
Description: The course of study is interdisciplinary, drawing heavily upon the resources of both the natural sciences and the health sciences faculties. Once admitted into the program, students spend three academic semesters at the university aaking program courses covering the areas of biochemistry, immunology, instrumentation, clinical chemistry, microbiology, blood banking, hematology, coagulation, parasitology, mycology, urinalysis, biomolecular techniques, medical genetics, and management. The last semester of the senior year is spent rotating through hospital laboratories affiliated with the program.
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Science (NAACLS). [3] Students that complete this program are eligible to sit for the American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) Board of Certification (BOC) examination. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music
Description: Pursue your passion for music with a Bachelor of Arts in Music from the University of New Haven. Explore our B.A. in Music program today ... Our Bachelor of Arts in Music program meetings you at your goals and aspires to pique your interests further and develop your capabilities. You will be guided and encouraged to channel your musical aptitude in a chosen direction and provided the enrichment of a liberal arts curriculum. Our graduates have pursued careers as performers, studio musicians, composers, music publishers, music critics and journalists, educators, curators, and librarians. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music & Sound Recording
Requirements: The University of New Haven's undergraduate admissions process is test-optional, meaning students can choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores. For applicants who choose not to submit test scores, a greater emphasis is placed on their high school GPA and the rigor of their coursework. All applicants, regardless of their decision to submit test scores, are considered for all forms of institutional aid.
Description: Technology pulsations are a constant in the ever-evolving world of music. Our Bachelor of Arts degree in Music & Sound Recording is built around the philosophy that to be a successful sound engineer, you must know the art form you are recording. To this end, our students take courses in three interrelated areas: music history, theory, and aesthetics; sound recording methodology and technique; and musicianship. Our faculty are former and current engineers, producers, and composers with professional expertise that informs our curriculum. Across all the courses in our program, students receive foundational skills in the generation and manipulation of sound, applying those skills in a variety of ways. You will have opportunities to enhance your development with courses on the theory and history of music.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $28,000 per year for first-year students and up to $25,000 per year for transfer students.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Industry
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the University of New Haven, first-year applicants must submit the following: a completed Common Application, an official high school transcript, one letter of recommendation (academic or other), and a personal essay or writing sample. The university has an application fee, but fee waivers are available for students who demonstrate financial need. The submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Music Industry is a dynamic program that provides the intellectual tools to address these questions and presents creative opportunities to learn from professionals to craft the answers. Students take a unique balance of courses that prepare you for technology-driven careers in record company operations, touring and concert promotion, artist management, marketing in the digital realm, music supervision, music publishing, and other industry roles. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Music Technology & Innovation
Requirements: Applicants that were homeschooled for a limited time during high school but have returned to a program through their district and plan to graduate through their district may follow our standard first-year student application process. Applicants that have transitioned from their district to a home-school program and will complete their high school education through a home-school program should follow the application process for a home-schooled teacher. Home-schooled students must indicate that they're completing high school through a home-school program on their application to the University. Official High School Transcript (Unofficial are acceptable to complete the application process, but official transcripts will be required for enrolling students.) Please note that the University of New Haven does not require test scores for most of our programs. [15]
Department: College of Arts and Sciences and Tagliatela College of Engineering

Description: There is no pause button in the evolving world of music technology or in music itself. So, how does the ongoing march of technology, with its ever-changing hardware and software, meld with the art of musical expression? This program shows you all the ways and prepares you to show the world as well. The future of music is where science intersects with art. [1] Our Bachelor of Science in Music Technology & Innovation combines skills in music and engineering to prepare students to be the leaders of our evolving sonic landscape. [1] Students in the program take courses in three interrelated areas: music history, theory, and aesthetics; sound recording methodology and technique; and musicianship. [1] In addition to these music and music technology courses, students choose on of two concentrations, which they pursue through courses in the University's Tagliatela College of Engineering. [1] At the end of the program, students bring together these interdisciplinary skills in a capstone project in music technology that demonstrates both a technical understanding of sound and a musical understanding of technology. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Music Technology and Innovation, Digital Systems Concentration
Requirements: All first-year candidates for undergraduate admission must submit the following: a completed Common Application or the UNewHaven Application, a $50 application fee, an official high school transcript, and an essay of 250-650 words. A letter of recommendation is optional. For those applying to Music programs, a portfolio submission is applicable.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in music technology and innovation provides students with a working knowledge of the sound recording industry, a solid foundation in music, and the technological skills to shape the future of the field. [3] Coursework focuses on three interrelated areas: 1) music theory, history, and aesthetics, 2) musicianship; and 3) sound recording methodology and technique. [3] Coursework for the BS in Music Technology and Innovation with a concentration in Digital Systems places a focus on the digital technology of sound through classes in computer programming, digital logic, and networking. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Music Technology and Innovation, Electronics Concentration
Requirements: The University of New Haven's website for first-year admissions does not specify a general application requirements text or description for all undergraduate programs. The application process is handled through the Common App, and specific requirements are detailed within that platform. The university is test-optional, and applicants can decide whether or not to submit their SAT or ACT scores.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in music technology and innovation provides students with a working knowledge of the sound recording industry, a solid foundation in music, and the technological skills to shape the future of the field. Coursework focuses on three interrelated areas: 1) music theory, history, and aesthetics, 2) musicianship; and 3) sound recording methodology and technique. Coursework for the BS in Music Technology and Innovation with a concentration in Electronics places a focus on the science and technology of recording through classes in calculus, physics, and electrical engineering.
CostPerCredit: $1,497 per credit (based on the 2024-2025 annual tuition of $44,910 divided by a standard 30 credits per year).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutrition Sciences
Requirements: For admission, first-year applicants must submit a completed application (the University of New Haven accepts the Common Application and the University of New Haven Application), an official high school transcript, and one letter of recommendation from a school counselor or teacher. An essay is also required. The university reviews applications on a rolling basis.

ProgramName: Associate of Science in Paramedicine
Requirements: In addition to general admission requirements for all prospective students, it is recommended that applicants to the paramedicine program demonstrate satisfactory performance in sciences and mathematics. It is strongly recommended that applicants have completed both high school biology and chemistry with laboratory and two years of high school algebra. An in-person or telephone interview with the program director may be required. Letters of recommendation supporting the student's ability to pursue a rigorous science-based curriculum and desire to contribute in the healthcare delivery system are strongly encouraged.
Description: Upon completion, the student will demonstrate the ability to comprehend, apply, and evaluate theoretical information relevant to their role of a patient-care provider in the field of pre-hospital emergency care as an EMT-Paramedic. The paramedic program will prepare the student to sit for the National Registry Certification Exam. Students graduate with certifications in Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS), Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS), Emergency Pediatric Care (EPC), Pre-hospital Trauma Life Support (PHTLS), Advanced Medical Life Support (AMLS), and Geriatric Emergency Medical Services (GEMS).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships, Need-based grants, Charger Blue and Gold Scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Paramedicine
Requirements: The University of New Haven has a test-optional policy for most undergraduate programs. Applicants can choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores. For those who do not submit scores, more emphasis is placed on the high school transcript, which is a required component of the application. The university recommends a strong college preparatory curriculum, including four years of English, three to four years of mathematics (including Algebra I, Geometry, and Algebra II), three to four years of science (including at least one lab science), two to three years of social sciences, and two to three years of a world language.
Description: A paramedic has a level of knowledge, skill, and treatment capabilities that are significantly beyond those of an Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) and which can dramatically improve a patient's outcome at the hospital. In response to the need for these uniquely trained emergency medical care professionals, the University of New Haven developed its paramedicine program. This program will prepare you to become a new breed of first responder – one who holds dual certification as both a firefighter and as a paramedic. Hands-on learning will be a major part of your education. You'll ride along with ambulance services and take patients' vitals. You'll practice doing chest compressions and starting IV lines on high-fidelity mannequins. You'll become part of teams who care for patients in whatever medical emergency unfolds. The goal of the paramedicine program is to make your education as real-world as it gets.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year students apply. This includes a completed application and official high school transcripts. The university conducts a holistic review of applications.
Description: The political science program focuses on learning by doing to encourage students to develop career skill sets, explore government and politics at all levels, and examine the relationship between political systems, institutions, actors, events, and organizations. The program focuses on key areas such as international relations, public policy, government affairs, the law, comparative politics, and american politial behavior. [4] Students in the B.A. political science program must complete 121 credits. [4] These courses must include 40 credits of University Core Curriculum, 42 credits of poltiical science major requirements, and 39 credits of free electives. [4] As a political science major at the University of New Haven, you will develop an understanding of our complex political system and its players, and explore how and where you can make an impact. [5] You will have the opportunity to conduct data-driven projects with well-respected researchers, learn the craft of politics from real policymakers, become a part of the University's award-winning Model United Nations team, explore the world through our study abroad programs to France, Japan, Germany, and England, and pursue a variety of internships in Washington, D.C., Hartford, and the New Haven area. [5]
Accredidation: The University of New Haven is accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE). [12, 13] Accreditation by the Commission applies to the institution as a whole and is not a guarantee of every course or program offered. [13] There is no mention of a specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Arts in Political Science program on the university's website.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Requirements: The University of New Haven utilizes the Common Application for first-year admissions. General application requirements typically include the completed Common Application, official high school transcripts, and at least one letter of recommendation. A personal essay, which is part of the Common Application, is also required.
Description: If you are drawn to the scientific study of human behavior in all of its myriad manifestations, you’ll thrive as a psychology major at the University of New Haven. You’ll learn to understand, and arrive at explanations for, a person’s thoughts and emotions. You’ll examine psychology from clinical, cognitive, developmental, personality, physiological, and social perspectives. Your classroom studies will then be brought to life in the laboratory and the clinic as well as in personal settings.
Accredidation: The University of New Haven is accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (formerly the Commission on Institutions of Higher Education of the New England Association of Schools and Colleges, Inc.), and has been since 1948. [11] Accreditation by the Commission is not partial but applies to the institution as a whole. ProgramName: Minor in Race and Ethnic Studies
Requirements: The minor in Race and Ethnic Studies is an interdisciplinary program offered in the College of Arts and Sciences. To provide students the tools and competencies to participate in a multi-racial and ethnic society and to be reflective about their racial and ethnic identities, the program provides students with a diversity of approaches to ethnicity and the concept of race in the United States and abroad. A student may minor in this program by completing 18 credits. [7] General requirements for minors include: at least 50% of the minor courses must be unduplicated, at least 50% of the minor courses must be completed in residence at UNH, and a minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in the minor. [7] A student may not declare a major and minor in the same program. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Sustainability Studies
Requirements: The minor in Sustainability Studies is directed toward students seeking to better understand environmental considerations in industry, government, non-profit, and academic institutions. Courses enhance students' major area of study by providing links between science, engineering, mathematics, business, economics, and the humanities. The minor takes a problem-solving approach to the discipline as students learn to apply broad knowledge to specific institutional, local, or global problems. 18 credit hours are required.

ProgramName: Minor in Systems Engineering
Requirements: To apply for the Minor in Systems Engineering, students must have a declared major on record. Applications need to be approved by the Minor Coordinator of the Division of Systems Engineering. It is recommended that students apply as early as possible, or by May 1 of their junior year. A minimum 2.00 GPA is required in the courses for the minor, with no grade being less than a C-. [1]
Description: TStudents may opt to take a minor in systems engineering by completing 18 credits. Curriculum covers current topics in systems engineering including system concepts, system thinking, system design, reliability, maintainability, design for manufacture and assembly, and quality program concepts, such as Six Sigma. The minor also strengthens knowledge in probability, statistics, and dealing with uncertainty and decision making in the design process. All course prerequisites must be met. [2]
